description.value: Small one-color proof of Mutual Broadcasting System advertisement. Illustration of dictionary-style book at center whose letter dividers spell ECONOMY. Text across book cover: WHO'S WHO IN U.S. RADIO / VOL 1 / ADVERTISERS. Below, a photoillustrated man in suit and hat with briefcase opens the front cover like a door. Printed text in open doorway lists names of brands such as Ovaltine, Lucky Strike, Illinois Meat, and Liberty Magazine. Printed text below illustration: NO LONGER JUST FOR THE CHOSEN SEVENTY-FIVE / During the past winter, only seventy-five advertisers on all networks were able to afford / hookups of 50 or more stations for their products. Significantly, the average weekly / expenditure of these was $8,000 an evening half hour. / Now Mutual's new Volume Plan-by removing the budget barrier that allowed only / the biggest to employ large scale broadcasting-opens the way to widespread network / success on a modest budget. Seventy-six station coverage of the country, reaching over / 200 of the leading 300 markets, is now available for only $3,438 an evening half hour. / MUTUAL BROADCASTING SYSTEM / WATCH THIS COOPERATIVE NETWORK OF INDEPENDENT STATIONS; Some discoloration at corners, edges, and over printed text.

legal.credit: Museum purchase with funding provided by the Buddy Taub Foundation, Dennis A. Roach and Jill Roach Directors

medium.value: Offset lithograph on glossy white paper

description.value: Design for an invitation to the Fortnum and Mason Spring fashion show. On cover fold, FORTNUM/AND/MASON, in three dimensional shaded dark green typography, printed over a hand-painted-looking sun and one half of a stylized leaf in chartreuse which is over printed in dark green, printed sideways, "Spring 1933."  The other half of this leaf is printed in dark green on the under sheet with "Collection" printed sideways in the opposite direction. Inside, printed on verso of cover fold and on under fold in dark and light green type, in separate type blocks, information on varieties of clothing, available colors, and date of the showing.

inscription.signed: Printed in chartreuse ink, at bottom corner of the leaf at lower right: EMCKK

medium.value: Color lithograph on heavy white wove paper

description.value: Study for a motif, likely for a book jacket cover. At center, contained within rough, square framing lines two hands holding what appear to be two circular coins (one with a face in profile, and the other with a constellation on it) and a compass. Below, in block lettering: WILLIAM A. M. BURDEN. Overlapping the bottom right corner of this composition, a second composition contained within its own square framing lines: an open book with a star on the left page, connected to a circle on the right page by a triangle.

description.value: Design for a composition, possibly a book cover, with a face depicted in gray. The facial features are depicted only on the left side, with the right side cast in shadow. From the figure’s eye, a single tear falls down their cheek. The figure’s hair is depicted with white streaks and a single white star at right. Behind the figure, the background in half yellow and half back. Image takes up only two-thirds of the page, with bottom third left blank.
